data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Atypical, decisive-experiment framing: the entire verdict question reduces to one measurable number \u2014 the probability p_n that a random 3-regular graph admits ANY locally stable mixed coloring reachable from a uniform start. Conjecture: p_n \u2192 p* with 0 < p* < 1, and the consensus probability equals 1 - p* + o(1), i.e. tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1. Obstruction structure: a locally stable mixed configuration is a two-coloring in which no vertex is in the minority among its neighborhood; every vertex agrees with the majority of its three neighbors; the color classes then have the property that each induced subgraph on a color class has minimum degree \u2265 2 (each vertex has at least 2 same-color neighbors), i.e. each color class spans a subgraph with min degree 2 \u2014 a union of cycles with chords. Quantitative law: the expected number of such bi-min-degree-2 splits on a random 3-regular graph grows exponentially in n (there are exponentially many, ~ (c\u221a2)^{n} candidates), but the fraction reachable from random initial conditions under the dynamics is \u0398(1): the fraction of the absorbing basin of mixed states among all initial colorings converges to a positive constant, giving the strictly-between verdict as n grows.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the branching-process coexistence probability computes to exactly 0 or 1, the strictly-between verdict fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If min-degree-2 induced splits do not exist whp (e.g. every 3-regular graph's only stable colorings are monochromatic), consensus probability tends to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If reachable mixed absorbing states have basin probability decaying like o(1), consensus probability tends to 1; if it grows like 1 - o(1), tends to 0.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Local stability \u27fa every vertex has \u22652 same-colored neighbors \u27fa each color class induces a minimum-degree-\u22652 spanning subgraph of the 3-regular graph, hence a union of disjoint cyclic cores joined by a matching of cross edges between the two colors. Random 3-regular graphs whp contain many such splits (e.g. take any 2-factor decomposition argument), so absorbing mixed states exist; but reachability is the filter: the asynchronous dynamics from a uniform coloring performs a local majority-annealing that lands in a mixed absorbing state only when initial color blocks percolate compatibly, an event with probability that has a limit strictly between 0 and 1 by a two-type branching-process survival calculation on the locally tree-like structure (supercritical for both colors, but coexistence of two surviving frozen basins has probability 1 - 2\u00b7q + q\u00b2\u00b7... landing strictly inside (0,1)).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
